subsystems.name: Telescope and light collection
subsystems.role: gathers photons from a star and its planet.

subsystems.name: Spectrograph
subsystems.role: splits light into wavelengths fine enough to resolve narrow molecular absorption lines.

subsystems.name: Starlight suppression
subsystems.role: blocks the star’s glare so the planet’s faint light can be measured.

subsystems.name: Detectors and calibration
subsystems.role: records spectra with very low noise.

subsystems.name: Data pipeline and atmospheric retrieval
subsystems.role: converts raw spectra into molecular abundances and tests alternative explanations.

subsystems.name: Target selection and observation planning
subsystems.role: chooses stars and planets where detection is feasible.

buildSteps.title: Choose target molecules and wavelengths
buildSteps.detail: Identify spectral features of industrial gases such as chlorofluorocarbons and nitrogen dioxide, and calculate the spectral resolution needed to see them.

buildSteps.title: Design the spectrograph
buildSteps.detail: Specify resolution, wavelength range, throughput and stability to match those features.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate optical components
buildSteps.detail: Polish mirrors, rule diffraction gratings and coat them for the required wavelength band.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and align the instrument
buildSteps.detail: Integrate optics and detectors, then test in vacuum and at operating temperature.

buildSteps.title: Develop retrieval software
buildSteps.detail: Build models that infer molecular abundances from spectra and quantify uncertainties.

buildSteps.title: Observe planets
buildSteps.detail: Use transiting or directly imaged planets, taking spectra during transit, eclipse or at high contrast.

buildSteps.title: Extract and analyze spectra
buildSteps.detail: Look for narrow absorption features at the predicted wavelengths.

buildSteps.title: Rule out false positives
buildSteps.detail: Test stellar activity, instrument systematics and any abiotic production routes for the same molecules.

buildSteps.title: Confirm detection
buildSteps.detail: Repeat with independent instruments or epochs and subject the result to peer review.

prerequisites.why: transmission and emission spectra of exoplanets have been measured, providing the basic method.
current coronagraphs cannot yet separate an Earth-like planet from its star at the needed contrast.
models exist but need improvement to reliably detect trace gases against noise and stellar contamination.
a dedicated space observatory with a large mirror and starlight suppression is needed to study Earth-like planets.
some pollutants such as nitrogen dioxide can have natural sources, so their production must be understood and ruled out.

pathway.milestone: JWST and ground-based telescopes search for industrial gases on transiting gas giants
pathway.unlocks: first upper limits and method development.

pathway.milestone: extremely large ground telescopes with high-resolution spectroscopy
pathway.unlocks: detection in nearby transiting planets and better discrimination from stellar signals.

pathway.milestone: a dedicated space mission to directly image Earth-like planets, such as the proposed Habitable Worlds Observatory
pathway.unlocks: spectra of potentially habitable worlds where chlorofluorocarbons would be unambiguous.
systematic surveys of many stars for technosignatures.
a credible technosignature detection rather than a single ambiguous measurement.
